rule_problems: Landed mode keeps a flier's target layer. The rule for modes[].mobility says: 'Leave it out when the mode keeps the unit's movement or cannot move at all'. Typed links define target as 'is this kind of target (from its mobility and size)'. So the landed Siege Chopper is still a low-air target in the coded data, while the wiki says ground weapons, fast tank hunters and mind control reach it there. Both coders followed the rule, and only the mode summary and a fit_note say otherwise. Proposed fix: let a mode that cannot move still give the ground it rests on, e.g. 'Leave out speed when the mode cannot move; still give mobility.base (or a new modes[].target) when the mode changes what kind of target the unit is, such as a flier that lands'. Kept as coded, with the fit_note at modes/0/mobility.

The combination check reads the base form only. The howitzer works only in the landed mode, but the validator tests 'weapon-families:artillery classes aircraft' against the unit's base class, so a ground-fired gun shows as artillery on an aircraft. Proposed fix: for a weapon with `mode`, check the family against the mode's class and mobility when the mode gives them (this needs the fix above, or a modes[].class rule for a landed flier). Kept as coded, recorded in atypical.

RA2 speed scale. The registry's Speed note says 'Ratio = unit land speed / 4', and speed_raw says 'unitless game values, such as the Command & Conquer Wiki's land speed, count'. ModEnc Speed/On_Unit_Types says infantry move at three-halves of their Speed value when not crawling. ModEnc's JumpjetSpeed page says jumpjet fliers move by a separate JumpjetSpeed key, and the ModEnc deployer pages discuss the chopper with jumpjet settings. The coded very-fast (3.0) would be fast (2.0) against the Conscript's real walking pace, and every RA2 vehicle and aircraft may be banded a step fast against infantry. Proposed fix: in games-r1 (and speed_reference), either set the RA2 reference to the Conscript's effective pace (Speed times three-halves) or state that raw Speed values are compared as given, and say whether the wiki's airspeed for jumpjet fliers is on that scale. Kept very-fast, with the uncertain entry at mobility/speed.

Anti-air from a hedged wiki line. roles.secondary counts it when 'a source calls it an anti-tank or anti-aircraft weapon'. The drop rule reads only 'official text' that 'calls a weak or limited point'. The anti-air trait is set exactly when can_target has high-air, and can_target lists kinds hit 'even a little'. The wiki says only that 'to some extent' it can serve as an AA weapon against Rocketeers, and that it lacks the firepower for Floating Discs, Kirovs and Harriers and has very little chance against AA vehicles. Yet the unit gets secondary anti-air and the anti-air trait, while the role reads 'Brings down aircraft, including jets and airships in high air'. Proposed fix: (a) a hedged phrase ('to some extent', 'can be used as') does not count as calling it an AA weapon; (b) drop a role, as with official weak text, when a cited source says the weapon is ineffective against the targets the role description names; (c) give the anti-air trait only when the sources do not call the weapon ineffective against high air, keeping high-air in can_target either way. Without anti-air, raider (very fast, light armour) would fill the slot. Kept [siege, anti-air], with the uncertain entry at roles/secondary.
